title: bonsai.pack/1
description: A pack's manifest, bonsai/pack.yaml (spec §5; format review 6.1): what Bonsai's engine reads from a pack beside what Claude Code loads from the plugin itself. Its id and version, what a machine needs, the files and settings lines the engine writes into a project, and what the pack declares besides its labels.yaml (bonsai.labels/1) and lanes.yaml (bonsai.lanes/1): its document kinds, its protected paths and, from set 8, its roles. At each update the engine copies its declarations into the lock's declares (spec §6), so bonsai check runs with no pack fetched. Lives in the pack's repository at bonsai/pack.yaml, beside the plugin's own folders. Written by the pack's maker; as a pack file it documents itself in # comments (contract §2.8), which bonsai check --pack keeps in step with the fields (step 5.1.9). Read by bonsai init and update at the locked commit, and by check --pack. Format-1 YAML (contract §2.4); this schema describes the file as a reader returns it (JSON). A writer writes every field below, in this order, null, [] or {} where it does not apply (contract §2.2); a reader treats a missing field as null, keeps an unknown one and refuses a duplicate key. A hook entry with no runs reads as [] (step 5.1.1).

format.description: The format and its version, always the first key (contract §2.2).

id.description: The pack's id: a lower-case letter, then lower-case letters, digits and dashes. It equals name in the plugin's .claude-plugin/plugin.json, so the pack's roles and skills load as <id>:<name> (spec §5). bonsai is Bonsai's own (its own hook lines go by it), so no pack takes it.

version.description: The pack's version, quoted. A release tag must equal it (spec §5: vX.Y.Z, or base-vX.Y.Z for base); the plugin's plugin.json never carries a version.

needs.description: What a machine needs for the pack; status --json lists each as a needs entry (contract §12).

claude_code.description: The oldest Claude Code the pack works with, a version, quoted; null for none. It raises Bonsai's own floor (spec §7); an older Claude Code gets a check warning, never a refusal.

block.description: The pack's part of the instruction block in the project's CLAUDE.md (file kind block): a file in the pack's bonsai/ folder, by its path there; null for none. Its docs stay in the pack: the block written into CLAUDE.md carries one pointer line (spec §5).

files.description: The files the engine writes into a project, each from the pack's bonsai/files/ (always-on protocol files and templates of kind once among them, spec §5); [] for none. A path may not be Bonsai's own (bonsai.yaml, .bonsai/), CLAUDE.md (kind block), or a place Claude Code or git loads on its own (a .claude or .claude-plugin folder, a .mcp.json, .lsp.json or .gitmodules file), letter case aside (step 5.1.1); a pack's roles, skills and hooks ride in its plugin.

path.description: Where the file goes in the project: project-relative, forward slashes, no leading slash. It may start with <protocols>/ as its first segment only (set 8; plan-5 5.5.0 note 1): the engine then writes the file under bonsai.yaml's documents.protocols, the folder the instruction block imports, and the lock records the resolved path, held to every rule another path is; no other <...> may appear anywhere in a path (bonsai check --pack refuses one). A pack cannot know a project's folder, so this is how an always-on protocol file reaches it.

from.description: Its source in the pack's bonsai/files/, forward slashes.

kind.description: How the engine treats it, a closed list: pack (Bonsai's; an edit in the project is a conflict) or once (written once, then the project's). The lock's other file kinds come from elsewhere: block from block, keys from hooks and deny, kept from the engine (bonsai.lock/1).

hooks.description: Hook lines the engine writes into the project's .claude/settings.json (file kind keys); [] for none. A hook line runs code: init and update write a new or changed one only with --allow-exec as well as --yes (spec §6, step 5.1.1). Bonsai's own hooks never ride in a plugin (spec §5).

examples.why: Prints the project's greeting when a session starts; it blocks nothing.

event.description: The Claude Code hook event (Claude Code's own list, so a plain string).

matcher.description: The event's matcher, or null for none.

command.description: The shell line Claude Code runs, quoted; it never calls bash by name (spec §3).

runs.description: The pack files the command runs, each by its path in the project (a files entry's path, this pack's or another linked pack's); [] for none. A change to one is code even when the line stays the same (spec §6); a command naming a linked pack's file that runs does not list is refused (step 5.1.1).

why.description: One plain sentence: what the line does, as update's preview prints it.
examples: Prints the project's greeting when a session starts; it blocks nothing.

deny.description: Deny rules the engine writes into the project's .claude/settings.json (file kind keys); [] for none.

examples.why: Agents cannot read the project's .env file.

rule.description: A Claude Code permission rule, quoted.

why.description: One plain sentence: what the rule stops, as update's preview prints it; bonsai check --pack requires it (spec §5).
examples: Agents cannot read the project's .env file.

documents.description: The document kinds the pack declares (contract §7.3): copied into the lock's declares and listed by status --json's documents with from set to this pack; [] for none. A project keeps each kind's place in its bonsai.yaml documents, under the kind's name.

kind.description: The kind's name, unique in the workspace; it is a key in bonsai.yaml's documents, so it has a key's form (contract §2.4).

path.description: The kind's default folder (one file per document, top level only), project-relative, which bonsai init writes into bonsai.yaml's documents and a project may change there; null for a kind that is one file.

file.description: The kind's default single file, project-relative, as path is; null for a kind that is a folder.

id.description: The pattern a document's id must match, a regular expression; an id resolves to exactly one file, never a path. null for a kind with no ids.

statuses.description: The kind's statuses: the pack's closed list for this kind, its one home (contract §2.2); the first is where a new document starts. [] for none.

person.description: The status moves a person makes, as [from, to] pairs (contract §10.2); [] for none.

agent.description: The status moves agents make, as [from, to] pairs; [] for none.

stamp.description: Fields set to the day's date when a document reaches a status, as {status: field}; {} for none.

task_field.description: The field naming the task a document belongs to (a plan's task:); null for none.

protected.description: Paths the pack declares protected (contract §5.5): an agent changes them only while its running task grants them. Globs, project-relative with forward slashes, copied into the lock's declares and applied beside bonsai.yaml's protected; [] for none. Base declares bonsai.yaml and the lock (contract §14).

roles.description: The roles the pack declares (set 8; Claude Code only: each role is a subagent of the plugin's, agents/<name>.md, which Claude Code loads as <pack id>:<name>): each one's name, its kind, whether the person's own session plays it, whether it may change files, Claude Code's maxTurns backstop, and its three limits, each with a default and a max. Copied into the lock's declares (roles), where the guard, bonsai message, status and check read them offline. A project sets its own default and max for any limit under the pack's entry in bonsai.yaml (bonsai.workspace/1's packs[].roles), and a brief any value up to the max in force (bonsai.message/1's budget). At most one role with session true across the packs a project links. bonsai check --pack holds each role to its file: agents/<name>.md is there, each file in agents/ is a declared role, and its maxTurns equals max_turns. A pack that declares none writes roles: [] (check --pack holds pack.yaml as its writer's file, contract §2.2).

name.description: The role's name: its file's in the plugin's agents/ folder (agents/<name>.md), so Claude Code loads it as <pack id>:<name>: a lower-case letter, then lower-case letters, digits and dashes. A message's address names it (bonsai.message/1's from and to).

kind.description: A lead, which may call helpers (through Claude Code's Agent tool, and resume one with SendMessage), or a helper, which calls no one: a closed list. The person's own session may call either.

session.description: true only for the role the person's own session plays (workflow's orchestrator): it is never a subagent, has no budget, and its address is the role's name alone; false for every other role.

writes.description: false for a role that changes nothing: the guard refuses it Claude Code's file tools (Edit, Write, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit) and the shell writes into the checkout it can read; true for a role that builds.

max_turns.description: Claude Code's maxTurns for the role, as its agents/<name>.md says it (check --pack holds the two equal): a backstop where the guard does not run (hooks turned off), set well above the limits (workflow sets four times the role's default actions), never the limit itself; null for none.

minutes.description: The role's minutes limit: minutes since the agent's first call, or since it tied its newest brief (its thinking before its first call is not counted; time idle between calls is). Its default is what an agent of the role gets when its brief names none, and its max the most a brief may give it; each a whole number, or null for no limit. A pack ships max equal to default; a project sets its own (bonsai.workspace/1's packs[].roles).

default.description: What an agent of this role gets when its brief names none; null for no limit.

max.description: The most a brief may give it; null for no limit.

actions.description: The role's actions limit: tool calls the agent makes, refused ones counted, from the same start. Its default is what an agent of the role gets when its brief names none, and its max the most a brief may give it; each a whole number, or null for no limit. A pack ships max equal to default; a project sets its own (bonsai.workspace/1's packs[].roles).

default.description: What an agent of this role gets when its brief names none; null for no limit.

max.description: The most a brief may give it; null for no limit.

red_runs.description: The role's red_runs limit: failed ladder runs in a row (a green climb sets the count back to 0; a new brief does not). Its default is what an agent of the role gets when its brief names none, and its max the most a brief may give it; each a whole number, or null for no limit. A pack ships max equal to default; a project sets its own (bonsai.workspace/1's packs[].roles).

default.description: What an agent of this role gets when its brief names none; null for no limit.

max.description: The most a brief may give it; null for no limit.
